task: Ranked spotlight portrait artwork (2:3 ideal) for ten ranked IDs
revision: 2 — weight optimisation of three heavy assets, primary visual review recorded, two caveat corrections
scope: Writes limited to dist/assets/portraits/*, dist/spotlight-portraits.json and this receipt. No git, no code, no other assets, no research/review decisions changed.
method: Direct download of official publisher art (Steam store CDN library_600x900_2x) for Steam titles, then exact-title box art for non-Steam titles: Internet Archive retail box scan (Diablo), LibRetro Thumbnails database box art (Halo CE, PES6), LaunchBox Games Database box-front scans (Skate 3, Simpsons Hit & Run). No upscaling, stretching, cropping, or AI generation: every file was the source bytes copied as-is; the only later operation on any of them is the proportional downscale recorded under derivatives. Dimensions were read with ffprobe (SOF/IHDR) at sourcing time and re-read with Pillow at optimisation time; sha256 is over the exact stored bytes. HTTP 200 alone was not treated as evidence of title match; identity is asserted from the source's own title metadata (Steam app id, IA file name, LibRetro file name, LaunchBox labeled box-front) plus the label's declared dimensions.

reviewDriver.note: The primary agent performed a visual review of the final on-disk cover files and accepted them. The verdicts in this section are the primary's; the optimisations and receipt corrections below were directed by the primary in the same review and implemented by the gameflexart worker, which ran no vision capability.

reviewDriver.verdict: All ten ranked portrait covers were viewed by the primary agent and accepted. No wrong-title, wrong-edition or unusable image was found. Identity claims below remain grounded in the cited source metadata; the visual review adds the primary's confirmation that each frame shows a genuine cover for the stated title.
correctionsDirected: The PES 6 source file is named '(Europe)' in the LibRetro database, but the image itself displays the Australia region packaging with a G rating. The actual visual region is Australia, so this receipt records Australia rather than repeating the filename's region (see the pes6 entry).
Do not assert that the Skate 3 fan project streams from a user's own copy beyond what the published catalogue already states (see the skate entry).
The Simpsons composite is normal asset preparation rather than fabrication: the portrait front cover was already available, so no panel crop was needed (see the simpsons entry).

The three oversized files (diablo, skate, simpsons) are far too heavy for 180px cards; each was reduced to a max-900px-height JPEG derivative, aspect preserved, high quality, with the source's dimensions/hash/bytes preserved alongside the derivative's recorded values.

derivatives.reason: The ranked cards render these covers at roughly 180px wide. The retained originals were 6.4MB/4352x5513 (diablo), 1.57MB/1517x2116 (skate) and 495629 bytes/1544x2156 (simpsons) — far more data than the card can display. Each was reduced once to a max-900px-height JPEG: aspect preserved, no crop, no stretch, no upscale, no AI.

processing.tool: Pillow 12.3.0 via the bundled Python at C:/Users/avizo/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/python/python.exe
processing.operation: open → convert('RGB') → resize to target height 900 with LANCZOS (width rounded from the source aspect ratio) → save JPEG quality 88, optimize, progressive, chroma subsampling 4:2:2; the source ICC profile is carried through when the source had one
processing.aspectRule: derivative width = round(source width × 900 ÷ source height); the pixel rounding is the only aspect deviation
processing.originalsPreserved: no original bytes were mutated in place; each original's dimensions, sha256 and byte count are recorded alongside its derivative's values in the entries below
processing.obsoleteFileRemoved: assets/portraits/diablo.png was deleted only after assets/portraits/diablo.jpg existed and had been verified in the portrait directory. It was an untracked (never committed) asset created by this same task, so removing it takes nothing out of history; the receipt's record of its bytes and hash is kept.

derivatives.notOptimisedByDesign: The five 600x900 JPEGs (bo1, quake3, webxash, vicecity, quake) are already small files at or near the display size; re-encoding them would spend a generation of quality for no useful saving, so they remain byte-identical to the sourced originals.

sha256 of every on-disk portrait file re-read after the writes and after the diablo.png removal

derivatives.limits: The re-encoded images were not inspected visually by this worker (it ran no vision capability). The metric used is the standard one — Lanczos downscale to a 900px height at quality 88 — and the primary's view of the pre-optimisation originals accepted the same covers.

Composite cropping is normal asset prep, not fabrication; it simply was not needed here. Only the proportional 900px-height downscale was applied (see derivatives).

summary.notes: All ten ranked IDs resolved to authentic exact-title portrait covers. No fallbacks to unrelated titles were required. The three heavy assets were reduced to max-900px-height JPEG derivatives, with every original's dimensions, hash and byte count preserved in this receipt.

implementerNotification.message: All 10 ranked spotlight portraits are sourced and stored. dist/spotlight-portraits.json maps each id to {src, sourceUrl, width, height}. Mixed formats: png for halo, pes6; jpeg for the rest. Consumers should set object-fit: cover; ratios range 0.667 (Steam 2:3) to 0.789 (Diablo full box front). diablo, skate and simpsons are stored as 900px-height JPEG derivatives, so no portrait file exceeds 646KB and the card-size render cost is bounded.
